task.title: Review network, CORS, and security limits
task.shortdesc: Review host, port, reload, health probes, CORS defaults, and security limits before making a source-run BPM instance reachable.

prereq.p: The source process can be started with make dev, and the administrator can change BPM_HOST, BPM_PORT, BPM_RELOAD, BPM_ENABLE_CORS, and BPM_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS.

context.p: Current defaults are optimized for local source operation: BPM_HOST="0.0.0.0", BPM_PORT="8000", BPM_RELOAD="true", BPM_ENABLE_CORS="true", and permissive origins equivalent to ["*"]. These defaults are not a hardened network exposure policy.

step.cmd: Choose the narrowest bind address for the current environment.

info.p: Use 127.0.0.1 for local Linux checks. Use 0.0.0.0 only when WSL browser forwarding or a controlled lab network requires it. Record the reason for any non-loopback binding.

step.cmd: Gate operational access with health and readiness probes.

info.p: Use GET /health and GET /health/ready before API examples or UI smoke checks. Successful probes show process liveness/readiness only; they do not prove database backup status, Firefox enforcement, authentication, authorization, or production topology.

step.cmd: Restrict CORS for any shared evaluation.

info.p: For local experiments, permissive BPM_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS may be acceptable. For a shared host, set explicit origins and record who owns the browser origin. BPM 0.9.0 documentation does not define credentialed CORS, CSRF protections, API authentication, or tenant isolation.

step.cmd: Keep unsupported security controls out of the BPM claim.

info.note: This release does not ship TLS termination, reverse proxy recipes, firewall policy, rate limiting, request signing, audit logging, SSO, OAuth/OIDC setup, role-based access control, vulnerability scanning, or HA failover. Document those as external controls if your environment adds them.

result.p: The source-run BPM network posture is documented as a controlled local or lab exposure rather than a production security architecture.

postreq.p: If probes fail or exposure is unclear, use the source-deployment verification topics before continuing with API integration examples.
